evidence: Default/selected "Priority" sort shows order: Review project proposal (High), Complete tax filing (High), Submit final report (High), Schedule dentist appointment (Medium), Buy groceries (Low) — High before Medium before Low.

Selecting "Deadline" sort ordered tasks ascending: Buy groceries (Aug26/Tomorrow), Review project proposal (Aug27), Submit final report (Aug30), Schedule dentist appointment (Sep1), Complete tax filing (Sep8), Write unit tests (Sep15).
Created task "Write unit tests" with just required fields present; active count increased from 5 to 6 and task appears in active list.

Created task with title "Write unit tests", description "Add tests for the new module", deadline 2026-09-15 (shown as Sep 15), priority High, prerequisite "Buy groceries" — all details retained and displayed on the created card.
Assigned "Buy groceries" as a prerequisite when creating "Write unit tests"; saved task displays "Prerequisite \"Buy groceries\" incomplete" confirming dependency was retained.

Tasks with incomplete prerequisites (Complete tax filing, Submit final report, Write unit tests) show disabled complete buttons ([disabled]) and warning labels; complete action unavailable while blocked.
Single incomplete prerequisite shown as 'Prerequisite "Review project proposal" incomplete' (Complete tax filing); multiple shown as '2 prerequisites incomplete' (Submit final report).

issue: Blocked task's edit control is fully disabled instead of allowing partial editing
actual: For blocked task "Complete tax filing" (prerequisite incomplete), the edit button is rendered with the disabled attribute and clicking it produces no response (no dialog opens, no fields become editable). Expected behavior per spec is that description and priority remain editable while title and deadline are locked; instead, the entire edit action is unavailable, so description and priority cannot be changed either.

evidence: Edited "Schedule dentist appointment": changed title→"Schedule dentist checkup", description, deadline 2026-09-01→2026-09-05, priority Medium→Low, added prerequisite "Buy groceries"; all changes persisted and displayed correctly. Then deleted the task; it disappeared from the list and active count dropped from 6 to 5.
Completed unblocked task "Buy groceries" (no prerequisites); it left the active list, active count dropped 5→4 and completed count rose 2→3.

Before completing "Buy groceries", dependent "Write unit tests" had disabled complete/edit buttons and warning "Prerequisite \"Buy groceries\" incomplete". After completing "Buy groceries", "Write unit tests" complete and edit buttons became enabled and label changed to "1 prerequisite completed".

Active tab shows 4 tasks with matching count "Active 4"; Completed tab shows 3 tasks (Buy groceries, Reply to client emails, Organize desk) with matching count "Completed 3"; switching updates the visible list accordingly.
After marking "Buy groceries" complete, it was not deleted — it appears in the Completed view with its details intact (title, priority, description, deadline).

Active tasks display title+priority always, description/deadline only when supplied (e.g. completed "Organize desk" shows no description/deadline paragraph, matching it had none). Blocked tasks expose prerequisite-incomplete labels. Completed tasks are visibly distinguished via CSS class "line-through text-muted-foreground" on the title, versus plain styling for active tasks.

Editing "Review project proposal" (which "Complete tax filing" directly depends on, and "Submit final report" indirectly depends on) shows a prerequisite selection list that excludes both "Complete tax filing" and "Submit final report" entirely — only "Write unit tests", "Buy groceries", "Organize desk", "Reply to client emails" are offered, preventing both direct and indirect cycles.
With title empty or filled with whitespace-only "   ", the "Create Task" button remains disabled, preventing submission; task list unchanged (still 4 active, 3 completed).

issue: Reopening a prerequisite of a completed dependent leaves the dependent simultaneously completed and blocked
actual: Completed "Write unit tests" (prerequisite: "Buy groceries", which was completed). Reopened "Buy groceries" from the Completed view — the app allowed this without warning. Afterward, "Write unit tests" remained in the Completed view (Completed count stayed part of the 3 completed tasks, active count 4 did not include it) while simultaneously displaying "Prerequisite \"Buy groceries\" incomplete" and having its reopen/edit buttons disabled. This is exactly the invalid state the item forbids: the dependent task is both completed (still listed under Completed) and blocked (shows unmet-prerequisite warning) at the same time. The system neither prevented reopening "Buy groceries" nor moved "Write unit tests" back to an incomplete state.

evidence: Hovering over "Prerequisite \"Review project proposal\" incomplete" on the "Complete tax filing" card revealed a tooltip titled "Dependency Chain" listing "Review project proposal — pending", identifying the specific pending prerequisite.

issue: Hovering the visual dashed connection line between dependent tasks does not trigger any dependency-chain popup
actual: The dashed connector between dependent task cards is rendered as an SVG path with class "stroke-warning/50" inside an <svg> that has CSS "pointer-events: none", so real mouse hovering over the visual line passes through to whatever is behind it (verified via document.elementFromPoint, which returned unrelated content divs, not the line). A small companion stub div (class "bg-dashed-line") near each card edge is the only real hoverable element in that area, but hovering it (verified with a real Playwright hover plus checking for any [role=tooltip] element) produced no popup at all. The dependency-chain popup only appears when hovering the blocked task's own warning label (see IX-20), not when hovering the connecting line itself, so the described interaction is not implemented.
